questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Career opportunities

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had Ghent and Utrecht on my list, and chose Ghent, since this exchange was a few weeks longer. It was important for me that I knew the university held a high standard and had a high equine case-load.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Had an amazing time! Learned a lot and got exactly what I wanted out of my exchange! Ghent is a beautiful city and I would warmly recommend an exchange there to everyone.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: In the beginning it was a little confusing, but once you got orientated at their website, you could find most information there. The international office in Ghent was also really kind and helpful to help if you had any questions, but expect a little waiting time on the emails, and the most important information we got sent out on email!

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had a welcome day at the faculty, and got plenty of information then. We also got assigned "mentors" you could ask if you had questions.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: The university/vet-international-office shared a bullet-point website where outgoing vet-students from Ghent could post their available housing, and I found it through there. Start looking in good time for housing!

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The campus is a fair bit outside of Ghent, so if you don't have a car - be prepared to bike a bit each day, the local transport isn't great. Or choose to live in Merelbeke, but then you have a bit into Ghent if you want to go in the evenings/weekends.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very happy with the housing I found.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I chose the equine course in my OLA, then I registered in OASIS and received emails from Ghent when I had to proceed with something. What I can remember now, I didn't find this too difficult. I had some problems getting my OLA into OASIS, but that got solved. Be patient with the registration process, it takes some time.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Tanya at the international office is very helpful! Also the help from UPCH was very good.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I applied in my online learning agreement that I wanted to do the equine rotation, and got an email later on that I was assigned that.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try to read up on their website as much as you can, I prepared myself as much as I could. Keep an eye out for updates on your email. Ask if needed! and again - be patient. :)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: They expect you to know what a last year students there know. But we got send out a list a few months before with skills we should know, so we could practice those before arrival if needed.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
I would say it's very similar. What I liked is that they do rounds in Ghent in the morning, where you learn about the patients, but also get quizzed about the diseases/clinical approach. I learned a lot through that! 
I experienced the case-load in the equine clinic is higher than in Copenhagen --> you will see more cases and different kinds of cases.
They give you a lot of freedom under responsibility. The 3 masters are responsible for the medicines on their own, drawing bloods, taking the anamnesis and first clinical examination of new patients, keeping an eye on critical patients during nights etc etc. I learned a lot through this.
We had practicals, both on internal medicine and surgery, where we got to e.g ultrasound abdomen, endoscope, castrate, distal limb ultrasound, they were great! All the vets were very kind and helpful, and liked when you asked questions.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Equine Clinical Rotation.

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would say, that if you want to integrate with the Belgian students and learn more, it is easier if you do one of the full programs and not the mixed one. When doing the mixed one, you never really learn how the departments roll and get to know people, and I experienced that those Erasmus students had a harder time at the clinic because of that.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: You need to rent scrubs at the clinic (20€/set), but you will get your money back once you leave.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: It's similar prices to Scandinavia.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were plenty available, also through the ESN, but I didn't do any (since clinic took a lot of time, and I explored the country on my own).

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: N/A

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Ghent, Bruge, Brussels, Knokke, Seaside/beach, Hallebos forest etc.

Do all the touristy stuff in Ghent - I loved the boat-tour!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I would say very easy. It was very smilar to the Scandinavian culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be open! I spent more time with local students than with Erasmus ones, and I met all of them in the clinic. Ask them questions about the course and the university, ask them about good tips in Ghent. I found all of them very welcoming and helpful.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I didn't experience any cultural differences during my exchange.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food, the history of the country and the people! I found Belgian people very welcoming.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Socialise with Belgian students and not only Erasmus students 
- Don't be afraid to ask them to speak in English! I doubled it a little in the beginning when they forgot, but if you keep on reminding, they will remember switch over more and more. I haven't experienced any problems with the language.
- If you're doing the equine course - look into the practicals! They don't really tell you about the ones on the surgical department, but you're allowed to sign up on Ufora, I did e.g. castrate a horse "on my own".

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
I had my car, and really enjoyed being able to explore the country a bit outside the cities. You don't need a car though, but for me it was really nice. 
The clinical guide you receive, wasn't really updated (at least this year). But it gives you a good baseline.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I had an amazing time from start to finish!! Super happy with the academic clinical course, with the city of Ghent, the Belgian culture and all new friends I have made. The vets were really good to explain and teach, and if you want - the opportunity to learn a lot is there. The case-load was high, and that means you do have a lot to do - but I also saw cases I never thought I would see in real life and that was really cool.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Coming as a new student and not knowing where stuff is in the clinic. Be proactive and ask them to show you a lot during your first weeks, this will make you more independent.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Go go go!! I can warmly recommend it!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
